title: A Guided City Walk
description: Four recordings from a walking tour of an old town: a welcome talk, a market visit, a chat between tourists and a talk about a clock tower.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Welcome to the tour
parts.intro: You will hear a guide called Tom at the start of a walking tour.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Good morning, everybody, and welcome to the Old Town walking tour. My name's Tom, and I'll be your guide for the next two hours.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Before we set off, a few practical things. We'll walk about three kilometres, but there are plenty of short stops, so it isn't tiring. If anyone needs a rest, just tell me.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: The tour usually finishes at the castle, but today the castle is closed for a private event. So instead, we'll end in the main square at around quarter past twelve, where there are lots of cafés.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Please stay together, because the streets in the old quarter are narrow and often crowded. I'll carry this green umbrella so you can always see me. And watch out for cyclists, who sometimes appear very suddenly.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Photographs are welcome everywhere except inside the cathedral, where they're not allowed during services. Finally, if you'd like to take a break for lunch, I can recommend a family restaurant near the square. It's a lovely sunny morning, so I think we're going to have a wonderful walk. Right, shall we begin?

parts.title: Part 2 · At the Silk Market
parts.intro: You will hear a guide, Lan, talking to a tourist, Mike, in a market.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: This is the Silk Market. It's been on this spot for more than three hundred years.

script.speaker: Mike
script.text: Excuse me, Lan. It doesn't look very old. The buildings seem quite modern.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Good question, Mike. The original market was destroyed in a fire in nineteen twenty. What you see now was rebuilt, but the layout is exactly the same.

script.speaker: Mike
script.text: I see. And do people still sell silk here?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Some do, but only about a quarter of the stalls. Most sell souvenirs now. If you want real silk, go to the stall at the very end, with the blue sign. The owner's family has made it for four generations.

script.speaker: Mike
script.text: Is it expensive?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: A scarf costs around twenty pounds, which is fair for something handmade. But be careful with the cheaper ones outside, because many are made from plastic.

script.speaker: Mike
script.text: Good to know. Can we try some of the street food too? I'm starving.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Of course. There's a baker over there selling coconut cakes. They're warm, and honestly, the best thing in the whole market. We'll stop for ten minutes, so you can also take some photographs of the old stalls.

parts.title: Part 3 · Plans for the afternoon
parts.intro: You will hear two tourists, Hannah and Nam, after the tour.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Well, that was better than I expected. I thought the guide would just read from a book.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Me too. Though I could have done without the long story about the bridge. I was getting a bit bored then.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Really? I loved that part. Anyway, what shall we do this afternoon? The museum closes at five.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Hmm. I'd like to see the museum, but my feet hurt. We walked much further than I thought.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: We could take the boat trip on the river instead. You can sit down, and you still see the city.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: That sounds good. How much is it?

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: I looked it up this morning. Twelve pounds each, or twenty for two people if you buy online.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Let's buy online, then. Does it say how long it takes?

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: About an hour. The last boat leaves at half past four, so we have plenty of time for lunch first.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Perfect. And we can visit the museum tomorrow morning when it's quieter.

parts.title: Part 4 · The clock tower
parts.intro: You will hear Lan, the guide, talking about a famous clock tower.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Now, if you look up, you'll see the famous clock tower. Many people think it's older than the cathedral, but it was actually finished in eighteen ninety.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: The tower was a gift from a rich merchant named Mr Dang. He wanted the people of the town to know the time, because at that time very few families could afford a watch.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: For almost fifty years the clock worked perfectly. Then, during a storm in nineteen thirty-six, lightning struck the tower and stopped it. The clock stayed silent for nearly two decades, and local people said it was bad luck.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: It was only repaired in the nineteen fifties, when a group of school children collected money by selling flowers. That is why you'll see a small flower carved above the door.

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Today the clock plays a short tune every day at noon. Many visitors wait for it, so I suggest we stand over there, on the left, where the view is clearer. I think the tune is a lovely way to end our tour.
